doc.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Why the bass is hard to record
summary: Moore explains the acoustic difficulty of recording the bass and how 1970s direct pickups gave a buzz-saw sound.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Well I’m probably a little more complicated to record than other bass players, not all other bass players, but modern bass players who use the whole instrument, the upper register. It’s hard to get an overall sounding bass. If you stay in one register, stay down in the low register, that’s kind of what you’re getting when you’re accompanying. And it’s almost like you’re recording two instruments, because it’s almost like playing two instruments. So what sounds good soloistically, doesn’t necessarily then — you’ve got to adjust it. It’s hard for me in a live situation to get a sound that sounds good for solos and accompaniment too. So it’s difficult to record, and the instrument’s hard on top of it. Any engineer I think will tell you it’s the hardest one to get because it’s soft. If you made a string long enough to vibrate that chamber it would be as tall as this room. I mean they made a bass violin where acoustically it was perfect, it takes two people to play it. Because you see the size of the chamber, think of the string on the violin, in proportion to the body, or a cello string in proportion to the body. You think now the same length of string for the body of the bass. It would take somebody on a ladder to play it. So acoustically you’re starting off—

A very imperfect instrument. And you’re always trying to get a big sound out of something that you’re not capable of really vibrating the whole thing. So it’s tough, it’s tough to record. And then in the 70s I did a lot of records and engineers went with the electronic pick-ups, and they got the worst bass sound of all during those periods, because it was easy for them, they didn’t have to worry about leakage from drums or anything else, they just plugged it directly into the board. And I can’t listen — there’s some records that I’m on where the music is really good, but I can’t listen to them © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

because of the sound of the instrument. It has a real hard, electric sound, not acoustic at all. And it’ll be the only instrument that sounds that way. The piano is okay, the drums are all right and everything else, and the bass sounds like a buzz saw or something.
